Benchmark Assigns Buy Rating to SiTime (SITM) Amid Timing Technology Market Expansion
On August 20, Gary Mobley from Benchmark initiated his coverage of SiTime Corp. (NASDAQ:SITM) with a target price of $850. The analyst assigned a Buy rating to the stock, backed by the expectations of increased relevance of precision timing for system manufacturers. Let's explore the underlying growth drivers and potential threats for a company that is considered as a technology disruptor within this space.
Q2 Growth, and the Renesas Deal's Impact
Mobley noted that challenges around system designs, as well as market forces, will be the key driving factors behind an enhanced relevance of precision semiconductor timing technology. The bullish case for SiTime also rests on Apple's increasing reliance on its internal cellular modems, switching from Qualcomm modems.
SiTime's net revenue in the second quarter reached $157.4 million, depicting an increase of 127% year-on-year. Each of the company's segments expanded by at least 50%, while CED line surged 181% compared to the same period in 2025. Adjusted gross margins were reported at 67.1%, while the adjusted net income clocked in at $65.6 million or $2.34 per diluted share. By the end of the quarter, SiTime carried $1,921 million in cash, equivalents and short-term investments. The cash position was bolstered by net proceeds from convertible notes, which were issued to finance the company's acquisition of Renesas Electronics' timing business.
The Renesas deal was finalized on July 1, and it will add more than 550 clocking products to SiTime's existing portfolio. This gives SiTime access to a highly reputable brand across clocking technology with a solid 30-year legacy of distinct products. Serving a customer base of more than 10,000, it is a financially sound business with sustained gross margins of around 70%. It generates close to 75% of its topline from the AI-Datacenter-Comms market, with the rest coming from automotive applications and industrials. Over the next 12 months the business is expected to bring in at least $300 million in revenue, which will likely increase further amid SiTime's go-to-market and sales competencies.
Integration Risk, Segment Concentration and Added Leverage
Renesas' deal comes with high integration risks since SiTime absorbs a much broader clocking portfolio, customer base and operations, which could create execution complexity and additional costs. SiTime's growth is heavily concentrated across its AI Datacenter Communications segment. This exposes it to the risk of potential decline in AI infrastructure capital investments.
Funding of the Renesas' deal through convertible senior notes leads to additional leverage and risk of possible dilution for existing shareholders. Additionally, the aggressive $300 million revenue forecast for the acquired business depends partly on successful post-acquisition sales and go-to-market execution, which is not guaranteed and might not be realized in case there are channel conflicts or customer overlap.
Institutional sentiment tracked across 1,000+ hedge funds by Insider Monkey reveals increasing amount of high-conviction backing for SiTime Corporation (NASDAQ:SITM), as smart-money managers raised their long-term exposure to the stock. As per 13F filing data, total number of hedge funds that held positions in the stock increased from 54 funds in Q1 2026 to 76 funds in Q2 2026.
With a short interest of 3.25%, there is not a significant amount of institutional skepticism around SiTime. FMR is the largest institutional owner in the stock as per Yahoo Finance database, with 3.97 million shares as of June 30. This translates into 13.20% of the company's total outstanding shares. Other notable institutional stakeholders include BlackRock and Vanguard Portfolio Management that held 7.95% and 4.03% stakes, respectively.
The Renesas deal carries strategic significance for SiTime, as it accelerates the company's path toward $1 billion mark. The transaction will also result in a tenfold expansion of SiTime's existing clocking portfolio, while solidifying its position in the fast-growing AI datacenter market, which is an increasingly important space for semiconductor companies. In line with Benchmark's recent rating, the company could generate annual revenue in the high-$100 million range, once Apple's entire product portfolio shifts from Qualcomm modems to Apple modems.

Benchmark Assigns Buy Rating to SiTime (SITM) Amid Timing Technology Market Expansion
On August 20, Gary Mobley from Benchmark initiated his coverage of SiTime Corp. (NASDAQ:SITM) with a target price of $850. The analyst assigned a Buy rating to the stock, backed by the expectations of increased relevance of precision timing for system manufacturers. Let's explore the underlying growth drivers and potential threats for a company that is considered as a technology disruptor within this space.
Q2 Growth, and the Renesas Deal's Impact
Mobley noted that challenges around system designs, as well as market forces, will be the key driving factors behind an enhanced relevance of precision semiconductor timing technology. The bullish case for SiTime also rests on Apple's increasing reliance on its internal cellular modems, switching from Qualcomm modems.
SiTime's net revenue in the second quarter reached $157.4 million, depicting an increase of 127% year-on-year. Each of the company's segments expanded by at least 50%, while CED line surged 181% compared to the same period in 2025. Adjusted gross margins were reported at 67.1%, while the adjusted net income clocked in at $65.6 million or $2.34 per diluted share. By the end of the quarter, SiTime carried $1,921 million in cash, equivalents and short-term investments. The cash position was bolstered by net proceeds from convertible notes, which were issued to finance the company's acquisition of Renesas Electronics' timing business.
The Renesas deal was finalized on July 1, and it will add more than 550 clocking products to SiTime's existing portfolio. This gives SiTime access to a highly reputable brand across clocking technology with a solid 30-year legacy of distinct products. Serving a customer base of more than 10,000, it is a financially sound business with sustained gross margins of around 70%. It generates close to 75% of its topline from the AI-Datacenter-Comms market, with the rest coming from automotive applications and industrials. Over the next 12 months the business is expected to bring in at least $300 million in revenue, which will likely increase further amid SiTime's go-to-market and sales competencies.
Integration Risk, Segment Concentration and Added Leverage
Renesas' deal comes with high integration risks since SiTime absorbs a much broader clocking portfolio, customer base and operations, which could create execution complexity and additional costs. SiTime's growth is heavily concentrated across its AI Datacenter Communications segment. This exposes it to the risk of potential decline in AI infrastructure capital investments.
Funding of the Renesas' deal through convertible senior notes leads to additional leverage and risk of possible dilution for existing shareholders. Additionally, the aggressive $300 million revenue forecast for the acquired business depends partly on successful post-acquisition sales and go-to-market execution, which is not guaranteed and might not be realized in case there are channel conflicts or customer overlap.
Institutional sentiment tracked across 1,000+ hedge funds by Insider Monkey reveals increasing amount of high-conviction backing for SiTime Corporation (NASDAQ:SITM), as smart-money managers raised their long-term exposure to the stock. As per 13F filing data, total number of hedge funds that held positions in the stock increased from 54 funds in Q1 2026 to 76 funds in Q2 2026.
With a short interest of 3.25%, there is not a significant amount of institutional skepticism around SiTime. FMR is the largest institutional owner in the stock as per Yahoo Finance database, with 3.97 million shares as of June 30. This translates into 13.20% of the company's total outstanding shares. Other notable institutional stakeholders include BlackRock and Vanguard Portfolio Management that held 7.95% and 4.03% stakes, respectively.
The Renesas deal carries strategic significance for SiTime, as it accelerates the company's path toward $1 billion mark. The transaction will also result in a tenfold expansion of SiTime's existing clocking portfolio, while solidifying its position in the fast-growing AI datacenter market, which is an increasingly important space for semiconductor companies. In line with Benchmark's recent rating, the company could generate annual revenue in the high-$100 million range, once Apple's entire product portfolio shifts from Qualcomm modems to Apple modems.

Zebra Technologies Earnings Call Signals Robust Upswing
Tipranks - Tipranks - Wed Aug 5, 7:18PM CDT
Zebra Technologies ((ZBRA)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.
Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks
Zebra Technologies delivered a notably upbeat earnings call, emphasizing record revenue, sharply higher earnings, and expanding margins. Management balanced this optimism with a frank discussion of memory supply risks, one‑time tariff benefits, and uneven regional performance, but reiterated confidence in structural demand drivers such as AI, machine vision, RFID, and healthcare.
Zebra reported quarterly sales above $1.5 billion, up 20.4% year over year and 9.2% on an organic basis. The performance exceeded the high end of guidance, signaling strong demand across its portfolio and effective execution despite supply chain complexities.
Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 27.7%, expanding 7.1 percentage points from a year ago, aided by a tariff recovery. Even excluding this $73 million benefit, margins improved by about 2 points, indicating underlying efficiency gains and better cost control.
Non‑GAAP diluted EPS came in at $6.35 for the quarter, a 76% increase versus last year. The figure was significantly above prior guidance, reflecting operating leverage from higher sales and margin expansion as well as disciplined expense management.
Adjusted gross margin rose roughly 540 basis points to 53.3%, driven largely by the IEEPA tariff recovery and favorable foreign‑exchange movements. While these one‑offs boosted profitability, management underscored that core margin improvement remains positive even without them.
The company raised full‑year sales growth guidance to 14%–16%, lifting the midpoint by 3 points, and now expects adjusted EBITDA margins of 23.5%–24%. Third‑quarter sales are projected to grow 17%–20%, with an EBITDA margin around 22%, supported by a strong backlog and recent momentum.
Year‑to‑date free cash flow reached $361 million, and full‑year free cash flow is expected to be at least $1 billion, implying roughly 100% conversion. Zebra repurchased $568 million of stock in the first half and plans around $150 million more in the second half, targeting about $700 million for the year.
Broad-Based End-Market and Regional Strength
End‑market demand was robust, with double‑digit growth in retail, manufacturing, and healthcare, the latter being the fastest‑growing sector. Regionally, North America grew 9%, EMEA 7%, Asia Pacific 13%, and Latin America 15%, underscoring a geographically diversified expansion.
Strategic Momentum in AI and Machine Vision
Zebra highlighted growing traction in AI‑powered frontline solutions and new AI‑optimized mobile devices. Machine vision outperformed expectations, helped by the Photoneo acquisition, while the Elo integration is driving early cross‑sell synergies estimated at about $10 million.
Supply-Chain Actions and Pricing Mitigation
The company has secured additional memory supply and fully offset a $20 million memory cost increase in Q2 through pricing and other actions. Expected pricing realization has been raised from roughly $60 million to $90 million to help counter an approximate $120 million memory headwind.
Management warned that memory supply remains dynamic and could constrain growth in the back half of 2026 and into 2027. Memory costs are expected to rise from Q2 to Q3, prompting continued mitigation efforts such as pricing adjustments, supplier qualification, and diversified sourcing.
A $73 million tariff recovery materially lifted Q2 gross margin and EBITDA, inflating reported profitability in the near term. Without this item, margin expansion is more modest, making clear that investors should adjust expectations for normalized performance in coming quarters.
Zebra guided Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin to around 22%, down from Q2 levels as the tariff refund rolls off and memory costs increase by roughly one point. The sequential step‑down highlights the impact of transient benefits and rising input costs on short‑term profitability.
Transportation and logistics sales were flat year over year, reflecting a tough comparison against strong prior‑year results. In EMEA, growth of 7% lagged other regions, with continued softness in the Middle East dampening overall momentum.
RFID revenue was flat in the quarter due to project timing and inherent deal volatility. Management still expects double‑digit RFID growth for the full year, but the Q2 performance underscores that individual project schedules can create near‑term swings.
Pricing Actions and Customer Sensitivities
The company has already implemented price increases to offset memory inflation and signaled that further actions may be needed. While necessary for protecting margins, these moves can be commercially sensitive and may face customer resistance if cost pressures persist.
Dependence on Multiple New Memory Suppliers
Zebra is qualifying many new memory suppliers and chip types, targeting five to seven qualified vendors per memory category. This diversification reduces single‑source risk but introduces execution challenges in ramping capacity and ensuring timely qualification through 2027.
Forward-Looking Guidance and Capital Strength
Looking ahead, management’s guidance assumes full mitigation of about $120 million in memory headwinds through pricing and operational actions. Strong free cash flow, modest net leverage around 1.9x, and ample credit capacity support ongoing investment, acquisitions, and share repurchases as Zebra pursues AI, machine vision, RFID, and healthcare growth.
Zebra’s latest earnings call painted a picture of a company firing on most cylinders, with record sales, surging EPS, and upgraded guidance. Investors must weigh the temporary nature of tariff benefits and ongoing memory‑related risks, but the underlying demand trends and strategic positioning suggest a favorable long‑term trajectory.

Zebra Technologies launches the new KC401 self-service kiosk.
Featuring a 10-inch display, the KC401 delivers a superior self-service experience for customers and frontline workers across the retail, hospitality, manufacturing, and healthcare industries delivering faster and more responsive self-service workflows.”
“As customer expectations for speed and convenience continue to grow, self-service technology serves as a defining feature of the modern store and other environments,” said James Poulton, Senior Vice President, Enterprise Mobile Computing, Zebra Technologies. “The KC401 provides a versatile, reliable solution for organizations to deliver the seamless, intuitive self-service experiences that their frontline workers and those they serve expect.”
The KC401 expands Zebra’s comprehensive self-service portfolio, including kiosks, mobile computers, and multipurpose touchscreens. With the integration of solutions from Elo, now part of Zebra, the expanded portfolio provides organizations across industries with a wider selection of versatile, high-performance products tailored to match their unique workflows.
Overcoming Friction for a Better Shopping Experience
New analysis from Coresight Research indicates a significant challenge in the retail industry, with more than 60% of retailers reporting that shoppers struggle to find products and navigate their stores. The KC401 directly addresses these hurdles, providing a digital touchpoint for shoppers to access product information like checking prices or inventory availability, and even view item availability, through an endless aisle experience.
According to the research, self-service solutions free up the capacity of about four associates per store on average, equaling about 22% of front-of-store labor capacity. Retailers can then reallocate this valuable time to higher-value activities like merchandising, returns, and in-store customer assistance.
Built for Durability, Seamless Deployment Across Frontline Operations
From the warehouse to the store floor, the KC401 is built for high-traffic environments. It withstands rigorous daily use across retail, hospitality, manufacturing and healthcare.
Enhanced with an impact-tested, scratch-resistant display, the kiosk can withstand everyday bumps and taps that are common in industrial environments, like manufacturing and warehousing.
Additionally, IP65-sealing protects against dust and liquids, allowing for frequent cleaning where hygiene standards are required, like restaurant kitchens or healthcare facilities.
An optional specialized scanner can simplify hands-free scanning workflows, making price and inventory checks, loyalty identification, and product returns more seamless.
The KC401 kiosk is also optimized with Zebra DNA and its comprehensive software suite of capabilities which simplifies device setup, security, and management. Zebra customers currently using the CC6000 kiosk can maintain operational continuity as the KC401 uses the same mounting solutions and infrastructure, enabling a cost-effective upgrade of digital touchpoints with minimal disruption.
The Zebra KC401 provides frontline workers and those they serve with superior self-service experiences.
The new kiosk is built to withstand high-traffic use and frequent cleaning, making it ideal for a wide range of applications across retail, hospitality, manufacturing, and healthcare.
Organizations benefit from an easy, flexible installation functioning as a drop-in replacement for existing CC6000 customers.

At the RAIN in Action Summit, the companies are illustrating how tags and readers with Gen2X support can improve reading performance in challenging real-world settings.
When Impinj introduced Gen2X – a standards-compatible enhancement to the RAIN RFID protocol that improves the performance of RFID solutions in real-world enterprise deployments – the company made it widely available to the RAIN industry, enabling manufacturers to add support to both new and already popular readers.
Today, Impinj has announced that intelligent operations leader Zebra is upgrading its portfolio of RFID handhelds, sleds, and fixed readers with support for Impinj Gen2X. Zebra is adding Gen2X support to improve handheld and overhead reading of hard-to-read items, boost the accuracy and speed of autonomous track-and-trace solutions in challenging conditions, and use RFID tags to help inhibit fraudulent items and returns.
At this week’s annual RAIN in Action Summit, Impinj and Zebra are demonstrating Gen2X performance on Zebra handheld devices, illustrating how tags and readers with Gen2X support can improve reading performance in challenging real-world settings. RFID tagging is now expanding into categories such as grocery, jewelry, health and beauty, and pharmaceuticals – product types that were historically difficult to tag and inventory, yet are important to achieving item-level visibility across enterprise operations.
Impinj developed Gen2X to address these real-world challenges and improve autonomous fixed reading solutions at enterprise scale, enabling reliable item visibility across small retail merchandise, densely packed items, and products containing liquids and metals. These innovations now support use cases ranging from supply chain traceability and overhead inventory visibility to self-checkout and loss prevention.
Extending RFID tagging to more items and use cases empowers enterprises to automate workflows using Physical Intelligence: the reliable realworld visibility enterprise AI systems need to see everything, waste nothing, and act instantly.
“As RAIN RFID adoption continues to scale across global enterprises, Zebra is focused on delivering innovations that improve real-world performance and usability,” states Chip Yager, vice president and general manager, Advanced Locationing Technology, Zebra Technologies. “By enabling Gen2X across our handhelds, sleds, and fixed readers, we’re helping customers achieve more reliable reads, faster inventory, and greater accuracy, especially in challenging environments.”
“Zebra was our first licensee for Gen2X, and we are excited to see this innovation expand across a wide range of Zebra handheld, sled, and fixed readers,” adds Gahan Richardson, executive vice president and general manager, Impinj. “Extending Gen2X across its portfolio, Zebra is helping enterprises obtain item-level visibility into a wider range of use cases, accelerating the adoption of RAIN RFID at scale.”
Zebra devices with Gen2X support are available now, including handhelds (MC33 family, TC22R, TC501, TC701), sleds (RFD40 family, RFD90 family), and fixed/overhead readers (FXR90, FX9600, FX7500, ATR7000). Gen2X capabilities will be available across Zebra’s RFID portfolio via seamless firmware upgrades.

Featuring a 10-inch display, the KC401 delivers a superior self-service experience for customers and frontline workers across the retail, hospitality, manufacturing, and healthcare industries delivering faster and more responsive self-service workflows."
"As customer expectations for speed and convenience continue to grow, self-service technology serves as a defining feature of the modern store and other environments," said James Poulton, Senior Vice President, Enterprise Mobile Computing, Zebra Technologies. With the integration of solutions from Elo, now part of Zebra, the expanded portfolio provides organizations across industries with a wider selection of versatile, high-performance products tailored to match their unique workflows.
Overcoming Friction for a Better Shopping Experience
New analysis from Coresight Research indicates a significant challenge in the retail industry, with more than 60% of retailers reporting that shoppers struggle to find products and navigate their stores. The KC401 directly addresses these hurdles, providing a digital touchpoint for shoppers to access product information like checking prices or inventory availability, and even view item availability, through an endless aisle experience.
According to the research, self-service solutions free up the capacity of about four associates per store on average, equaling about 22% of front-of-store labor capacity. Retailers can then reallocate this valuable time to higher-value activities like merchandising, returns, and in-store customer assistance.
Built for Durability, Seamless Deployment Across Frontline Operations
From the warehouse to the store floor, the KC401 is built for high-traffic environments. It withstands rigorous daily use across retail, hospitality, manufacturing and healthcare.
Enhanced with an impact-tested, scratch-resistant display, the kiosk can withstand everyday bumps and taps that are common in industrial environments, like manufacturing and warehousing.
Additionally, IP65-sealing protects against dust and liquids, allowing for frequent cleaning where hygiene standards are required, like restaurant kitchens or healthcare facilities.
An optional specialized scanner can simplify hands-free scanning workflows, making price and inventory checks, loyalty identification, and product returns more seamless.
The KC401 kiosk is also optimized with Zebra DNA and its comprehensive software suite of capabilities which simplifies device setup, security, and management. Zebra customers currently using the CC6000 kiosk can maintain operational continuity as the KC401 uses the same mounting solutions and infrastructure, enabling a cost-effective upgrade of digital touchpoints with minimal disruption.

Zebra Technologies Earnings Call Signals Robust Upswing
Tipranks - Tipranks - Wed Aug 5, 7:18PM CDT
Zebra Technologies ((ZBRA)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.
Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks
Zebra Technologies delivered a notably upbeat earnings call, emphasizing record revenue, sharply higher earnings, and expanding margins. Management balanced this optimism with a frank discussion of memory supply risks, one‑time tariff benefits, and uneven regional performance, but reiterated confidence in structural demand drivers such as AI, machine vision, RFID, and healthcare.
Zebra reported quarterly sales above $1.5 billion, up 20.4% year over year and 9.2% on an organic basis. The performance exceeded the high end of guidance, signaling strong demand across its portfolio and effective execution despite supply chain complexities.
Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 27.7%, expanding 7.1 percentage points from a year ago, aided by a tariff recovery. Even excluding this $73 million benefit, margins improved by about 2 points, indicating underlying efficiency gains and better cost control.
Non‑GAAP diluted EPS came in at $6.35 for the quarter, a 76% increase versus last year. The figure was significantly above prior guidance, reflecting operating leverage from higher sales and margin expansion as well as disciplined expense management.
Adjusted gross margin rose roughly 540 basis points to 53.3%, driven largely by the IEEPA tariff recovery and favorable foreign‑exchange movements. While these one‑offs boosted profitability, management underscored that core margin improvement remains positive even without them.
The company raised full‑year sales growth guidance to 14%–16%, lifting the midpoint by 3 points, and now expects adjusted EBITDA margins of 23.5%–24%. Third‑quarter sales are projected to grow 17%–20%, with an EBITDA margin around 22%, supported by a strong backlog and recent momentum.
Year‑to‑date free cash flow reached $361 million, and full‑year free cash flow is expected to be at least $1 billion, implying roughly 100% conversion. Zebra repurchased $568 million of stock in the first half and plans around $150 million more in the second half, targeting about $700 million for the year.
Broad-Based End-Market and Regional Strength
End‑market demand was robust, with double‑digit growth in retail, manufacturing, and healthcare, the latter being the fastest‑growing sector. Regionally, North America grew 9%, EMEA 7%, Asia Pacific 13%, and Latin America 15%, underscoring a geographically diversified expansion.
Strategic Momentum in AI and Machine Vision
Zebra highlighted growing traction in AI‑powered frontline solutions and new AI‑optimized mobile devices. Machine vision outperformed expectations, helped by the Photoneo acquisition, while the Elo integration is driving early cross‑sell synergies estimated at about $10 million.
Supply-Chain Actions and Pricing Mitigation
The company has secured additional memory supply and fully offset a $20 million memory cost increase in Q2 through pricing and other actions. Expected pricing realization has been raised from roughly $60 million to $90 million to help counter an approximate $120 million memory headwind.
Management warned that memory supply remains dynamic and could constrain growth in the back half of 2026 and into 2027. Memory costs are expected to rise from Q2 to Q3, prompting continued mitigation efforts such as pricing adjustments, supplier qualification, and diversified sourcing.
A $73 million tariff recovery materially lifted Q2 gross margin and EBITDA, inflating reported profitability in the near term. Without this item, margin expansion is more modest, making clear that investors should adjust expectations for normalized performance in coming quarters.
Zebra guided Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin to around 22%, down from Q2 levels as the tariff refund rolls off and memory costs increase by roughly one point. The sequential step‑down highlights the impact of transient benefits and rising input costs on short‑term profitability.
Transportation and logistics sales were flat year over year, reflecting a tough comparison against strong prior‑year results. In EMEA, growth of 7% lagged other regions, with continued softness in the Middle East dampening overall momentum.
RFID revenue was flat in the quarter due to project timing and inherent deal volatility. Management still expects double‑digit RFID growth for the full year, but the Q2 performance underscores that individual project schedules can create near‑term swings.
Pricing Actions and Customer Sensitivities
The company has already implemented price increases to offset memory inflation and signaled that further actions may be needed. While necessary for protecting margins, these moves can be commercially sensitive and may face customer resistance if cost pressures persist.
Dependence on Multiple New Memory Suppliers
Zebra is qualifying many new memory suppliers and chip types, targeting five to seven qualified vendors per memory category. This diversification reduces single‑source risk but introduces execution challenges in ramping capacity and ensuring timely qualification through 2027.
Forward-Looking Guidance and Capital Strength
Looking ahead, management’s guidance assumes full mitigation of about $120 million in memory headwinds through pricing and operational actions. Strong free cash flow, modest net leverage around 1.9x, and ample credit capacity support ongoing investment, acquisitions, and share repurchases as Zebra pursues AI, machine vision, RFID, and healthcare growth.
Zebra’s latest earnings call painted a picture of a company firing on most cylinders, with record sales, surging EPS, and upgraded guidance. Investors must weigh the temporary nature of tariff benefits and ongoing memory‑related risks, but the underlying demand trends and strategic positioning suggest a favorable long‑term trajectory.

Zebra Technologies Introduces KC401 Kiosk to Drive Smarter Self-Service Across Industries
New Android-based device empowers frontline teams by automating routine tasks, reclaiming critical labor capacity and elevating customer service
LINCOLNSHIRE, Ill.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Sep. 17, 2026-- Zebra Technologies Corporation (NASDAQ: ZBRA), a global leader in digitizing and automating workflows to enable intelligent operations, today announced the launch of the KC401 kiosk, purpose-built to handle routine inquiries, eliminating workflow bottlenecks, reducing queue times, and freeing up staff for higher-value customer and patient interactions.
This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260917768873/en/
Zebra Technologies launches the new KC401 self-service kiosk.
Featuring a 10-inch display, the KC401 delivers a superior self-service experience for customers and frontline workers across the retail, hospitality, manufacturing, and healthcare industries delivering faster and more responsive self-service workflows.”
“As customer expectations for speed and convenience continue to grow, self-service technology serves as a defining feature of the modern store and other environments,” said James Poulton, Senior Vice President, Enterprise Mobile Computing, Zebra Technologies. “The KC401 provides a versatile, reliable solution for organizations to deliver the seamless, intuitive self-service experiences that their frontline workers and those they serve expect.”
The KC401 expands Zebra’s comprehensive self-service portfolio, including kiosks, mobile computers, and multipurpose touchscreens. With the integration of solutions from Elo, now part of Zebra, the expanded portfolio provides organizations across industries with a wider selection of versatile, high-performance products tailored to match their unique workflows.
Overcoming Friction for a Better Shopping Experience
New analysis from Coresight Research indicates a significant challenge in the retail industry, with more than 60% of retailers reporting that shoppers struggle to find products and navigate their stores. The KC401 directly addresses these hurdles, providing a digital touchpoint for shoppers to access product information like checking prices or inventory availability, and even view item availability, through an endless aisle experience.
According to the research, self-service solutions free up the capacity of about four associates per store on average, equaling about 22% of front-of-store labor capacity. Retailers can then reallocate this valuable time to higher-value activities like merchandising, returns, and in-store customer assistance.
Built for Durability, Seamless Deployment Across Frontline Operations
From the warehouse to the store floor, the KC401 is built for high-traffic environments. It withstands rigorous daily use across retail, hospitality, manufacturing and healthcare.
Enhanced with an impact-tested, scratch-resistant display, the kiosk can withstand everyday bumps and taps that are common in industrial environments, like manufacturing and warehousing.
Additionally, IP65-sealing protects against dust and liquids, allowing for frequent cleaning where hygiene standards are required, like restaurant kitchens or healthcare facilities.
An optional specialized scanner can simplify hands-free scanning workflows, making price and inventory checks, loyalty identification, and product returns more seamless.
The KC401 kiosk is also optimized with Zebra DNA and its comprehensive software suite of capabilities which simplifies device setup, security, and management. Zebra customers currently using the CC6000 kiosk can maintain operational continuity as the KC401 uses the same mounting solutions and infrastructure, enabling a cost-effective upgrade of digital touchpoints with minimal disruption.
The Zebra KC401 provides frontline workers and those they serve with superior self-service experiences.
The new kiosk is built to withstand high-traffic use and frequent cleaning, making it ideal for a wide range of applications across retail, hospitality, manufacturing, and healthcare.
Organizations benefit from an easy, flexible installation functioning as a drop-in replacement for existing CC6000 customers.

Zebra Technologies upgrades RFID readers with Impinj Gen2X technology
At the RAIN in Action Summit, the companies are illustrating how tags and readers with Gen2X support can improve reading performance in challenging real-world settings.
When Impinj introduced Gen2X – a standards-compatible enhancement to the RAIN RFID protocol that improves the performance of RFID solutions in real-world enterprise deployments – the company made it widely available to the RAIN industry, enabling manufacturers to add support to both new and already popular readers.
Today, Impinj has announced that intelligent operations leader Zebra is upgrading its portfolio of RFID handhelds, sleds, and fixed readers with support for Impinj Gen2X. Zebra is adding Gen2X support to improve handheld and overhead reading of hard-to-read items, boost the accuracy and speed of autonomous track-and-trace solutions in challenging conditions, and use RFID tags to help inhibit fraudulent items and returns.
At this week’s annual RAIN in Action Summit, Impinj and Zebra are demonstrating Gen2X performance on Zebra handheld devices, illustrating how tags and readers with Gen2X support can improve reading performance in challenging real-world settings. RFID tagging is now expanding into categories such as grocery, jewelry, health and beauty, and pharmaceuticals – product types that were historically difficult to tag and inventory, yet are important to achieving item-level visibility across enterprise operations.
Impinj developed Gen2X to address these real-world challenges and improve autonomous fixed reading solutions at enterprise scale, enabling reliable item visibility across small retail merchandise, densely packed items, and products containing liquids and metals. These innovations now support use cases ranging from supply chain traceability and overhead inventory visibility to self-checkout and loss prevention.
Extending RFID tagging to more items and use cases empowers enterprises to automate workflows using Physical Intelligence: the reliable realworld visibility enterprise AI systems need to see everything, waste nothing, and act instantly.
“As RAIN RFID adoption continues to scale across global enterprises, Zebra is focused on delivering innovations that improve real-world performance and usability,” states Chip Yager, vice president and general manager, Advanced Locationing Technology, Zebra Technologies. “By enabling Gen2X across our handhelds, sleds, and fixed readers, we’re helping customers achieve more reliable reads, faster inventory, and greater accuracy, especially in challenging environments.”
“Zebra was our first licensee for Gen2X, and we are excited to see this innovation expand across a wide range of Zebra handheld, sled, and fixed readers,” adds Gahan Richardson, executive vice president and general manager, Impinj. “Extending Gen2X across its portfolio, Zebra is helping enterprises obtain item-level visibility into a wider range of use cases, accelerating the adoption of RAIN RFID at scale.”
Zebra devices with Gen2X support are available now, including handhelds (MC33 family, TC22R, TC501, TC701), sleds (RFD40 family, RFD90 family), and fixed/overhead readers (FXR90, FX9600, FX7500, ATR7000). Gen2X capabilities will be available across Zebra’s RFID portfolio via seamless firmware upgrades.

LINCOLNSHIRE, Ill., September 23, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Zebra Technologies Corporation (NASDAQ: ZBRA), a global leader in digitizing and automating workflows to deliver intelligent operations, today announced its participation in the 6th United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) Digital Health Symposium this week at Seton Hall University. Tom Bianculli, Chief Technology Officer at Zebra Technologies, will deliver a keynote address focused on the importance of creating intelligent, connected healthcare ecosystems.
Bianculli's keynote titled, "From Vision to Velocity: Powering SL2-10X with Frontline AI and Orchestrated Care," will detail Zebra's strategy to move artificial intelligence (AI) from the back-office to the point of care. He will address how Frontline AI, which leverages on-device intelligence and real-time sensing, is essential for building the operational scaffolding to make the industry's "Stay Left, Shift Left-10x" (SL2-10X) vision an executable reality.
The presentation will detail how Zebra's Orchestrated Care framework connects providers, patients, and administrators to achieve this SL2-10X transformation. Zebra's Orchestrated Care approach aims to improve clinical workflows, enhance patient safety, and deliver better outcomes through real-time data, point-of-care mobility and ecosystem-wide collaboration.
"Technology must be the catalyst for a more connected and intelligent future. At the UNGA Digital Health Symposium, we will share our vision for Frontline AI that moves beyond the cloud to empower clinicians and administrators at the point of care," said Bianculli. "By integrating frontline AI with real-time asset visibility, we can minimize the estimated 30% of nursing hours lost to administrative tasks and create a system that is more efficient and fundamentally more human-centric."

Zebra Technologies Introduces KC401 Kiosk to Drive Smarter Self-Service Across Industries
Zebra Technologies launches the new KC401 self-service kiosk.
New Android-based device empowers frontline teams by automating routine tasks, reclaiming critical labor capacity and elevating customer service
LINCOLNSHIRE, Ill., September 17, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Zebra Technologies Corporation (NASDAQ: ZBRA), a global leader in digitizing and automating workflows to enable intelligent operations, today announced the launch of the KC401 kiosk, purpose-built to handle routine inquiries, eliminating workflow bottlenecks, reducing queue times, and freeing up staff for higher-value customer and patient interactions.
Featuring a 10-inch display, the KC401 delivers a superior self-service experience for customers and frontline workers across the retail, hospitality, manufacturing, and healthcare industries delivering faster and more responsive self-service workflows."
"As customer expectations for speed and convenience continue to grow, self-service technology serves as a defining feature of the modern store and other environments," said James Poulton, Senior Vice President, Enterprise Mobile Computing, Zebra Technologies. "The KC401 provides a versatile, reliable solution for organizations to deliver the seamless, intuitive self-service experiences that their frontline workers and those they serve expect."
The KC401 expands Zebra's comprehensive self-service portfolio, including kiosks, mobile computers, and multipurpose touchscreens. With the integration of solutions from Elo, now part of Zebra, the expanded portfolio provides organizations across industries with a wider selection of versatile, high-performance products tailored to match their unique workflows.
Overcoming Friction for a Better Shopping Experience
New analysis from Coresight Research indicates a significant challenge in the retail industry, with more than 60% of retailers reporting that shoppers struggle to find products and navigate their stores. The KC401 directly addresses these hurdles, providing a digital touchpoint for shoppers to access product information like checking prices or inventory availability, and even view item availability, through an endless aisle experience.
According to the research, self-service solutions free up the capacity of about four associates per store on average, equaling about 22% of front-of-store labor capacity. Retailers can then reallocate this valuable time to higher-value activities like merchandising, returns, and in-store customer assistance.
Built for Durability, Seamless Deployment Across Frontline Operations
From the warehouse to the store floor, the KC401 is built for high-traffic environments. It withstands rigorous daily use across retail, hospitality, manufacturing and healthcare.
Enhanced with an impact-tested, scratch-resistant display, the kiosk can withstand everyday bumps and taps that are common in industrial environments, like manufacturing and warehousing.
Additionally, IP65-sealing protects against dust and liquids, allowing for frequent cleaning where hygiene standards are required, like restaurant kitchens or healthcare facilities.
An optional specialized scanner can simplify hands-free scanning workflows, making price and inventory checks, loyalty identification, and product returns more seamless.
The KC401 kiosk is also optimized with Zebra DNA and its comprehensive software suite of capabilities which simplifies device setup, security, and management. Zebra customers currently using the CC6000 kiosk can maintain operational continuity as the KC401 uses the same mounting solutions and infrastructure, enabling a cost-effective upgrade of digital touchpoints with minimal disruption.
The Zebra KC401 provides frontline workers and those they serve with superior self-service experiences.
The new kiosk is built to withstand high-traffic use and frequent cleaning, making it ideal for a wide range of applications across retail, hospitality, manufacturing, and healthcare.
Organizations benefit from an easy, flexible installation functioning as a drop-in replacement for existing CC6000 customers.

Fundamentally, the latest quarter gives the backdrop for the current valuation: Zebra reported adjusted earnings per share of USD 6.35 for the second quarter of 2026, beating analyst estimates by 46 percent and prompting management to raise its full-year adjusted EPS guidance to a range of USD 20.75 to USD 21.25, according to Yahoo Finance.
As Yahoo Finance notes, despite this sizeable earnings beat and upgraded outlook, Zebra Technologies stock has fallen about 4.9 percent since the earnings release, suggesting that broader market conditions and sector sentiment are weighing on the share price more than company-specific fundamentals.
Over a longer horizon, performance remains robust: trailing total-return data as of September 9, 2026 show Zebra up 44.70 percent year to date and 12.55 percent over one year, compared with 11.80 percent and 17.51 percent respectively for the S&P 500, indicating that the stock has outperformed the benchmark in 2026 even if it lags over the past three years, according to Yahoo Finance.

The conference also shed light on Zebra’s capital allocation and balance-sheet strategy. At the same time, management described memory-chip inflation as a key near-term headwind and explained that Zebra is mitigating this pressure with early pricing actions and direct relationships with the top three memory vendors; the company moved its 2026 price realization guidance from USD 60 million up to USD 90 million and indicated it would still prefer a scenario where USD 120 million of cost relief offsets USD 90 million of price gains, which would leave EPS about USD 30 million better off, as outlined by Investing.com.
For investors, that combination of strong cash generation, sizeable buybacks and disciplined pricing around inflation-sensitive components means that leverage to memory prices is a central risk factor, but one that Zebra is actively managing through supplier diversification, early bidding on contracts and broader automation and AI-led revenue drivers, according to the same Investing.com transcript.

Is Zebra Technologies (ZBRA) A Bargain As University Health Deployment Lifts Its Automation Story?
Zebra Technologies (ZBRA) is back in focus after University Health rolled out its mobile computers and printers across inpatient units, reshaping bedside workflows and giving investors a fresh real world case study.
Recent trading has been choppy. The share price is down about 9% over the past month and 3% over the past week, yet a 47% 90 day share price return and 38% year to date gain suggest momentum has been rebuilding after a weaker stretch.
Over the past year, total shareholder return of 7.6% contrasts with a three year total shareholder return of 35.9%, while the five year total shareholder return is down 36.9%. Zebra Technologies is still in the process of repairing a longer track record, even as fresh contract wins, industry awards and an upcoming Citi Global TMT appearance keep the story in front of investors.
Look beyond Zebra Technologies and identify other automation heavyweights by screening for 38 robotics and automation stocks that may be benefiting from similar demand in healthcare, logistics, and smart manufacturing.
The share price reset and fresh contract wins leave Zebra Technologies caught between a repaired story and a demanding chart. Does that recent run still leave enough upside for new buyers on today's valuation multiples?
On the most followed narrative, Zebra Technologies screens as undervalued, with a fair value of $399 against a last close of $342.73, which puts the focus squarely on how durable its automation and software story really is.
The accelerating shift toward automation, digital transformation, and real-time workflow optimization, driven by ongoing labor shortages, e-commerce expansion, and increased supply chain demands, continues to fuel robust demand for Zebra's portfolio (hardware, software, RFID, machine vision), supporting sustained revenue growth and long-term earnings visibility.
See why 26 investors see Zebra Technologies as 14% undervalued.
The narrative relies on a 9.39% discount rate to bring those future cash flows back to today, which is a relatively demanding hurdle for any automation supplier. It also assumes earnings move from $539.0m to $991.3m over time and that the stock trades on a 20.1x P/E on those future profits, compared with a higher multiple today and a 31.8x figure for the wider US Electronic industry.
For readers, the key test is whether that combination of earnings growth, higher margins and a lower future P/E feels realistic while Zebra Technologies is still working through softer recent earnings, declining net margins and higher debt. The narrative view is that embedded devices, services and software across retail, logistics and healthcare can underpin cash flows strongly enough to justify both the fair value of $399 and the 14.1% gap to the current share price.
Result: Fair Value of $399 (UNDERVALUED)
Still, the bullish Zebra Technologies script frays quickly if trade policy turns less friendly or if hardware heavy revenue leaves earnings more exposed to cyclical slowdowns.

Zebra Technologies Announces Second Quarter 2026 Results
Delivers record performance with broad-based growth across segments and regions
Lincolnshire, Ill., August 4, 2026 — Zebra Technologies Corporation (NASDAQ: ZBRA), a global leader in digitizing and automating workflows to deliver intelligent operations, today announced results for the second quarter ended July 4, 2026.
•Net sales of $1,557 million; year-over-year increase of 20.4%
•Net income of $233 million and net income per diluted share of $4.85
•Non-GAAP diluted EPS increased year-over-year to $6.35
•Adjusted EBITDA increased year-over-year to $431 million
•Recorded IEEPA tariff recoveries of $73 million, of which $14 million received in the quarter
“Our record results reflect broad-based demand for our innovative solutions and excellent execution on our growth and profitability priorities. We delivered for our customers by leveraging our long-standing supplier relationships to support our growth," said Bill Burns, Chief Executive Officer of Zebra Technologies. "The momentum we see across our business underscores Zebra's position as the foundation for intelligent operations and frontline AI as customers digitize and automate environments."
"Our strong balance sheet and cash flow continue to provide significant financial flexibility, enabling us to invest for growth while returning more than $560 million to shareholders in the first half of the year through disciplined share repurchases," said Nathan Winters, Chief Financial Officer of Zebra Technologies. "We believe this balanced approach positions Zebra to create long-term shareholder value."

Second Quarter 2026 Compared to the Second Quarter 2025
Net sales were $1,557 million compared to $1,293 million in the prior year. Net sales in the Connected Frontline ("CF") segment were $903 million compared to $717 million in the prior year. Asset Visibility & Automation ("AVA") segment net sales were $654 million compared to $576 million in the prior year. Consolidated organic net sales increased 9.2% year-over-year, with a 7.5% increase in the CF segment and an 11.4% increase in the AVA segment.
Gross profit was $825 million compared to $616 million in the prior year. Gross margin increased to 53.0% compared to 47.6% in the prior year primarily due to IEEPA tariff recoveries and favorable foreign currency exchange. Adjusted gross margin was 53.3% compared to 47.9% in the prior year.
Operating expenses increased to $504 million from $433 million in the prior year primarily due to expenses associated with acquired businesses including amortization of intangible assets. Adjusted operating expenses increased to $419 million from $370 million in the prior year.
Net income was $233 million, or $4.85 per diluted share, compared to net income of $112 million, or $2.19 per diluted share, in the prior year. Non-GAAP net income increased to $305 million or $6.35 per diluted share, compared to $186 million, or $3.61 per diluted share for the prior year.
Adjusted EBITDA increased to $431 million, or 27.7% of adjusted net sales, compared to $267 million, or 20.6% of adjusted net sales in the prior year.
As of July 4, 2026, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $157 million and total debt of $2,776 million.
For the first six months of 2026, net cash provided by operating activities was $387 million and the Company invested $26 million in capital expenditures, resulting in free cash flow of $361 million. The Company also made share repurchases of $568 million.
Mr. Burns added, "Strong demand momentum and progress on productivity and memory supply supports our significantly increased outlook for the full year. We are focused on driving sustainable growth across our business with our innovative portfolio of solutions, as we continue to benefit from trends in automation and Physical AI."
The Company expects third quarter sales growth between 17% and 20% compared to the prior year. This expectation includes approximately 10.5 points of favorable impact from business acquisitions, dispositions and foreign currency.
Adjusted EBITDA margin for the third quarter is expected to be approximately 22%. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share are expected to be in the range of $4.70 to $4.90. This assumes an adjusted effective tax rate of approximately 19%.
The Company expects full year sales growth between 14% and 16% compared to the prior year. This expectation includes approximately 8 points of favorable impact from business acquisitions, dispositions and foreign currency.
Adjusted EBITDA margin for the full year is expected to be between 23.5% and 24.0%. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share are expected to be in the range of $20.75 to $21.25. This assumes an adjusted effective tax rate of approximately 19%.
Free Cash Flow for the full year is expected to be greater than $1 billion.

Investors are invited to listen to a live webcast of Zebra’s conference call regarding the Company’s financial results. The conference call will be held today at 7:30 a.m. Central Time (8:30 a.m. Eastern Time). To view the webcast, visit the investor relations section of the Company’s website at investors.zebra.com.
Who is Zebra Technologies?
Zebra (NASDAQ: ZBRA) provides the foundation for intelligent operations with an award-winning portfolio of connected frontline, asset visibility and automation solutions which empower our customers to deploy AI on the frontline. Organizations globally across retail, manufacturing, transportation, logistics, healthcare, and other industries rely on us to deliver outcomes today while driving innovation for what’s next. Together with our partners, we create new ways of working that improve productivity and empower organizations to be better every day. Learn more at www.zebra.com.
Follow Zebra on our Blog, LinkedIn, Facebook, X, Instagram and YouTube.

Topaz is optimized for PON Fiber Gateways, Ethernet, and Fixed Wireless Access (FWA) deployments. It provides processing performance, memory bandwidth, and connectivity required for next-generation gateways, including Wi-Fi 8, and AI-enabled services, while enabling upgrades to future multi-gigabit access technologies beyond 10G. Built with a secure-by-design approach, Topaz is designed to support compliance with leading cybersecurity frameworks and regulations, including NIST IR 8425A (U.S.), Radio Equipment Directive (RED), and the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) (EU).
From a technology differentiation perspective Topaz combines broadband access, packet processing, AI acceleration, advanced security, intelligent power management, and low-latency networking technologies such as L4S and Dual-Queue AQM into a single highly integrated SoC. This integration reduces system complexity, lowers BOM costs, and accelerates product development while enabling differentiated operator services.
The Topaz family provides a scalable portfolio that allows OEMs and operators to optimize system cost and performance for specific applications, ranging from cost-efficient residential gateways to premium multi-gigabit, converged broadband platforms. A common architecture across the family enables extensive hardware and software reuse while preserving flexibility to address diverse market requirements.
Sharing a common software and hardware foundation with MaxLinear's Puma™ 9 DOCSIS® platform, Topaz enables significant code, feature, and development reuse across Cable, Fiber, Ethernet, and FWA product portfolios. This unified platform approach, also known as AnyWAN, shortens software development cycles, simplifies portfolio management, and helps operators rapidly adopt new technologies while reducing engineering investment and long-term support costs.
Purpose-Built for 10G PON & Beyond: Delivers high-efficiency performance for current 10G deployments while establishing a scalable, long-term architecture for next-generation tiers. High-speed 25G and 50G connectivity, DDR5 memory support, and low latency packet processing are designed to provide long-term headroom for network growth.
Wi-Fi 8 Ready Infrastructure: Provides the high processing performance, memory bandwidth, and interconnect speeds required to drive deterministic, ultra-low-latency Wi-Fi 8 wireless networks. Topaz handles dense, multi-gigabit traffic across connected home and business environments while minimizing bottlenecks.
All-in-One High-Integration SoC: Consolidates multi-gigabit fiber access, packet routing, AI/ML acceleration, and advanced security on a single chip. This single-chip design can eliminate the need for separate multi-processor architectures, lowering bill-of-materials (BOM) costs, reducing physical design footprints, and shortening development cycles.
Low Power Consumption: Features integrated PHYs and Dynamic Power Management (DPM) technology that dynamically scales energy use based on real-time traffic loads. The SoC minimizes power during idle periods while maintaining instant line-rate responsiveness, helping operators meet strict ERP mandates and sustainability goals.
Hardware-Grade Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Readiness: Optimized for the long deployment lifecycles associated with fiber infrastructure investments, Topaz incorporates advanced hardware-based security technologies and readiness for post-quantum cryptography (PQC). The platform helps operators address emerging cyber threats, evolving security regulations, and requirements such as the European Cyber Resilience Act (CRA).
Open Ecosystem & Unified Software: Designed around open standards, especially those championed by the prpl Foundation’s prplWare, as well as supporting RDK, Topaz provides maximum application portability. Sharing a common architecture with MaxLinear’s Puma 9 DOCSIS® platform, the device allows operators and OEMs to unify cable and fiber gateway codebases.
AI & Next-Gen Service Acceleration: Integrates local compute and AI/ML engines to power intelligent edge services allowing both local as well as hybrid solutions together with extended cloud processing. AI-assisted home network diagnostics including preemptive analysis, pre-processed and compressed network statistics as well as AI-enabled security and QoS optimize the operators’ network operations and provide improved customer quality of experience.
Optimized for Low Latency: The upgraded packet processing engine is optimized to minimize packet delay inside the gateway. The accelerated data path now also includes a hardware-based dual-queue AQM implementation for L4S, bridging the gap between new L4S-enabled services and the network infrastructure.
“ Operators can’t afford to wait years to upgrade their network infrastructure to meet demands of the AI-driven broadband home,” said Puneet Sethi, Senior Vice President and General Manager, Network Infrastructure and Carrier, at MaxLinear. “ Customers want smart, AI-powered applications for home and business services, but they don’t want to pay a premium for inflated power bills or monthly service fees to make it happen. With Topaz, we are solving for both. Our latest platform not only delivers affordable 10G PON connectivity today, it’s also flexible enough to accelerate operators into the future – without compromising on power efficiency.”
“The broadband gateway market continues to demand greater performance, lower power consumption, and faster product development cycles,”said Robert Lin, CEO Askey. “Topaz combines advanced fiber connectivity, AI acceleration, and future-ready networking capabilities within a highly integrated architecture. We believe this platform has the potential to help OEMs deliver innovative gateway solutions while reducing complexity and development costs. We are happy to be early access partner for Topaz and looking forward to incorporating Topaz in our roadmap as industry transitions to AI-enabled broadband services.”
"The convergence of multi-gigabit fiber access, advanced Wi-Fi, and AI-driven services is creating new requirements for broadband gateway platforms,"said James Lee, CEO, Gemtek Technology Co., Ltd. "The Topaz platform is built to provide the processing performance, security, memory bandwidth, and integration needed to support next-generation broadband and Wi-Fi deployments and differentiated operator services. We are excited to work with MaxLinear and leverage Topaz to accelerate innovation for our global customers."
Select OEMs are already designing next-generation gateways with Topaz. By consolidating key broadband, Wi-Fi, security, and processing functions into a single highly integrated platform, Topaz enables operators to deliver superior subscriber experiences while reducing system complexity, lowering power consumption, and improving overall cost efficiency.
MaxLinear will be attending Network X 2026 in Vienna, Austria. Visit us at Booth D21 to see the debut of Topaz, our next-generation PON home gateway platform, and learn how we're enabling the future of broadband connectivity.

Maxlinear Inc. (NASDAQ:MXL) climbed to a three-month high on Friday, adding 15 percent to close at $105.93 apiece, as investors began positioning portfolios ahead of the release of its earnings performance in the third quarter of the year.
Week on week, the stock rose by 12.88 percent.

Late last month, Maxlinear Inc. (NASDAQ:MXL) launched a new unified semiconductor solution that enables broadband operators to deliver D4.0/D3.1+ multi-gigabit services, power Edge AI, personal AI and Wi-Fi 8 connectivity while helping them reduce costs.

Shares of MaxLinear (MXL +3.61%) gained 50.7% in September 2026, according to data from S&P Global Market Intelligence. The fabless semiconductor designer is up 549% over the past year as of Oct. 2.
Three things drove last month's surge.
There's accelerating demand for the optical networking chips that link AI data centers.
MaxLinear got some bullish analyst reports.
The stock completed a rebound from summer lows around $60.
A sharp pullback in the middle of the month had more to do with the chip sector as a whole than with MaxLinear itself.
Image source: Getty Images.
AI data center demand lifted MaxLinear shares
MaxLinear makes digital signal processors, or DSPs, that sit inside the optical modules connecting servers in AI data centers. That's a lucrative business as tech giants are building AI data centers as fast as regulators and budgets will allow.
Management has raised its optical data center outlook in each of the last three quarters. The company started the year saying that business would top $100 million, and the midpoint of current guidance is $220 million.
Speaking at a technology conference on Sept. 9, CFO Steven Litchfield noted that chip prices are holding firm. Lead times for new orders are 26 to 28 weeks and MaxLinear's customers are currently setting up deliveries for the spring of 2027.
"I don't anticipate pricing coming down much between now and the end of next year," Litchfield said. "The market continues to grow."
The company is indeed firmly attached to the AI boom, and specifically to the related AI data center construction megatrend. MaxLinear holds no more than 7% of the optical module market, and Litchfield hopes to roughly triple that footprint over the next 2-3 years. If management is even half right, that's a lot of room for near-term growth.
Add a positive credit outlook from S&P Global Ratings on Sept. 11, price targets of $125 from StoneX and $120 from Stifel, and a bounce from summer lows near $60, and MaxLinear's shares had plenty of tailwinds last month.
The surge included one troubling dip, though. MaxLinear slid about 9% from Sept. 11 to Sept. 14, alongside chip peers such as Rambus and Allegro MicroSystems.
AI security events made investors worry about slower software development and lower AI hardware requirements. The trough didn't last long, but the high-tech corner of Wall Street got a healthy reminder of security concerns.

The catch behind MaxLinear's big September
Before anyone calls this a victory lap, the bounce comes with a few asterisks.
MaxLinear's stock has essentially moved sideways from early May to the start of October amid a macro-driven summer slump. It's a volatile name, and investors should be prepared for continued speed bumps given lofty valuation multiples.
Trading at 39 times forward earnings estimates, MaxLinear makes high-priced stocks like Credo (22.7x) and Broadcom (18.4x) look affordable.
There's no denying that MaxLinear's management has ambitious growth plans, but the stock is a risky bet. I'll certainly watch for MaxLinear's Q3 report on Oct. 28, but I'm not slamming the "buy" button right now.

CARLSBAD, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Sep 28, 2026--
MaxLinear, Inc. (Nasdaq: MXL), a leading provider of communications semiconductors for broadband, connectivity, and infrastructure applications, today announced Puma™ 9, a next-generation DOCSIS® platform designed to help broadband operators accelerate the rollout of D4.0/D3.1+ multi-gigabit services, power Edge AI, personal AI and Wi-Fi 8 connectivity while also helping operators to reduce their cost and complexity of transitioning to DOCSIS 4.0.
This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260928528178/en/
Puma™ 9 helps operators accelerate DOCSIS 4.0 deployment while reducing CPE costs, preserving investments, and enabling a flexible upgrade path from DOCSIS 3.1 to 4.0.
Puma 9 brings advanced Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) security readiness and DDR5 memory compatibility, helping operators protect their networks against future threats and avoid supply chain risk associated with legacy memory types. Built with a secure-by-design approach, Puma 9 is designed to support compliance with leading cybersecurity frameworks and regulations, including NIST IR 8425A (U.S.), Radio Equipment Directive (RED), and the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) (EU).
Operators are facing expanding demands that extend far beyond raw bandwidth. From Edge AI and Personal AI to Wi-Fi 8, heightened security requirements, and tighter capital budgets, success increasingly depends on the ability to evolve services without constantly replacing hardware. Puma 9 reimagines the gateway lifecycle, helping operators maximize existing DOCSIS 3.1 investments while preparing for next-generation services. Through flexible in-field upgrades, operators can deliver multi-gigabit experiences on their own timeline without frequent hardware refreshes or costly requalification cycles.
With a high level of integration in 8nm process technology, Puma 9 is the first and only platform that can support DOCSIS 3.1, DOCSIS 3.1+, and DOCSIS 4.0 standards on a single SoC without incurring significant cost additions. By unifying these capabilities into a highly integrated architecture, Puma 9 enables operators to reduce their spending today while providing a path to accelerate new services, reduce deployment complexity, and maximize infrastructure investments.
Key features in Puma 9 help bridge gaps in network economics and flexibility for DOCSIS deployments:
Post-Quantum Security Readiness: Enabled with Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) technology to help operators secure their broadband networks against emerging post-quantum threats.
Next-Gen Memory Technology: Industry’s only DOCSIS platform compatible with DDR5 memory, allowing for greater memory supplier flexibility and a longer lifecycle for the platform.
Wi-Fi 8 Integration: Provides a scalable foundation for next-generation Wi-Fi 8 gateways, delivering low latency and processing headroom needed for AI-driven applications.
Flexibility Across Evolving Standards: Support for DOCSIS 3.1, 3.1+, and 4.0 standards enabled on a single platform. Allows easy in-field upgrades and maximizes return on investment over time.
Leading 3.1+ Performance: With support for 5x OFDM channels, delivers greater than 10 Gbps of downstream throughput – higher than many other DOCSIS 3.1 solutions available today.
Integrated Edge AI Processing: MaxAI™-powered NPU enhances QoS, optimizes networks, improves user experiences, and lowers operational costs.
Addressing the DOCSIS 4.0/3.1 Upgrade Dilemma
As operators prepare for a new wave of growth fueled by Edge AI, personalized AI services, Wi-Fi 8, and increasing demand for uninterrupted multi-gigabit speeds, they face a significant challenge: existing solutions typically require expensive DOCSIS 4.0 CPE refreshes and qualification cycles. To manage costs, many operators delay CPE investments until broader network upgrades are underway. This approach not only increases the financial stress on operators but also takes away the flexibility to offer D4.0 surgically in those markets where competitive pressure or consumers demand it sooner than other markets. Long and costly D4.0 qualification cycles and expensive D4.0 CPE HW deployments take the flexibility and competitive advantage away from DOCSIS operators.
Operators are also contending with growing supply chain uncertainty as major memory vendors transition away from DDR4. Dependence on DDR4-only D4.0 CPE introduces further price pressure and significant longevity risk, as broadband equipment requires stable component availability and support throughout extended product lifecycles.
Puma 9 addresses both challenges by optimizing CPE cost to enable a software-driven migration path from DOCSIS 3.1 to DOCSIS 3.1+ and/or to DOCSIS 4.0 through in-field upgrades. Puma 9-based designs offer CPE cost parity with existing D3.1 CPE costs. This enables operators to deploy a highly capable DOCSIS platform without incurring additional CPE spend. That means operators can now deploy DOCSIS 4.0-ready devices today, preserve their investments, and upgrade to D4.0 or D3.1+ only when their business requires it—without costly truck rolls, expensive HW/SW investments, or large-scale equipment replacement programs. Further, Puma 9 supports five OFDM channels in D3.1+ configuration. This allows operators to offer 12 Gbps, i.e., a D4.0-like experience, over existing D3.1 networks. This further accelerates time to better consumer experiences and enables operators to phase their network spend.
“ When planning their next-gen network and CPE upgrades, operators require flexibility above all else," said Jeff Heynen, Vice President, Broadband Access and Home Networking, Dell'Oro Group. "Operators are looking to proactively manage their spending on next-gen upgrades, which is now becoming more of a focus because of the DDR supply situation. Having the flexibility to separate the timing of network and CPE spends, eliminating long SW qualification cycles with a single CPE platform that is backward and forward compatible, enabling CPE upgrade while meeting legacy CPE HW costs – all these items materially lower operators’ deployment risk and capital expenses, and allow them to spend exactly where they need to be competitive."
A recent Dell’Oro industry forecast indicates that DOCSIS 4.0 and fiber expansion investments are entering a new spending cycle that is expected to peak in 2028, while escalating residential gateway costs remain a concern for operators. Puma 9 was designed specifically for this environment, enabling operators to align CPE investments with network evolution while significantly reducing deployment costs.
Puma 9 helps operators accelerate DOCSIS 4.0 adoption with a highly integrated platform that lowers deployment costs, extends the value of existing software investments, and provides a flexible migration path to future broadband services. By enabling a flexible, operator-driven migration strategy, Puma 9 minimizes upgrade risk, enhances deployment agility, and positions operators to capitalize on long-term broadband growth opportunities.
Investment-Preserving Architecture: A single platform supports DOCSIS 3.1, DOCSIS 3.1+, and DOCSIS 4.0, allowing operators to deploy hardware once and evolve capabilities over time through in-field software upgrades. This approach extends platform value, reduces hardware replacement cycles, and aligns infrastructure investments with network evolution and customer demand.
Leading Performance: With five OFDM channel support, Puma 9 supports up to 12 Gbps downstream throughput. That allows operators to provide DOCSIS 4.0-class experiences over existing DOCSIS 3.1 networks today and give them the capacity needed for future multi-gigabit service plans.
Lower Deployment Costs: Designed with a highly integrated architecture, Puma 9 can reduce customer premises equipment costs by 30% to 50% compared with alternative DOCSIS 4.0 solutions, improving deployment economics and accelerating service rollouts.
Proven Broadband Foundation: Built on MaxLinear's field-proven DOCSIS 4.0 front-end technology and mature DOCSIS and voice software already deployed worldwide, helping reduce implementation risk and speed time to market.
"Operators are looking for a smarter path to DOCSIS 4.0—one that minimizes cost and risk while maximizing the value of today's investments," said Puneet Sethi, SVP & GM of MaxLinear’s Network Infrastructure and Carrier Business Unit. "Puma 9 significantly changes those economics to benefit operators and consumers. Operators can now deploy DOCSIS 4.0-ready equipment today without expanding their CPE budget allocation, enabling them to offer higher speeds to consumers who need it. Puma 9 also offers 12 Gbps in D3.1+ mode, which enables D4.0 experience over a D3.1 network, enabling operators to phase their network upgrade spend without compromising consumer experience."
“Over the past decades, together with our partner MaxLinear, we have enabled operators and consumers to benefit from an unmatched broadband experience – one that consumers now associate with FRITZ!," said Diego Friedel, Vice President of Software at FRITZ!."With FRITZ!’s software expertise, our focus has always been on continuously improving the consumer experience through new broadband technologies, including DOCSIS. We are excited to learn about the Puma 9 platform and its capabilities, and we look forward to evaluating it in our lab."
" At Askey, we are committed to delivering commercial-ready broadband platforms that simplify operator deployments while enabling next-generation connected-home experiences," said Eric Lui, R&D VP of Askey. "By combining Wi-Fi 8, AI processing, post-quantum security readiness, and a forward-looking DOCSIS architecture, Puma 9 gives us the foundation to deliver platforms that support new revenue-generating services while meeting long-term customer needs. We're developing our next generation of gateways on the Puma 9 platform to help operators create a scalable, future-proof solution that accelerates service innovation, optimizes deployment costs, and seamlessly supports evolving subscriber demands."
"Delivering scalable, long-life CPE requires architectural flexibility from the silicon up," said James Lee, President, Gemtek."We are leveraging MaxLinear's Puma 9 platform to develop next-generation DOCSIS and Wi-Fi gateways that help operators meet growing bandwidth demands while simplifying technology transitions over time. With support for DDR5 memory, post-quantum cryptography readiness, and future broadband upgrades, Puma 9 enables us to deliver solutions that maximize performance today and protect operator investments well into the future."
"Mediacom is always evaluating technologies that can help us balance performance, flexibility, and reliability," said JR Walden, SVP Technology and CTO of Mediacom Communications. "The ability to deploy a platform that supports DOCSIS 3.1+, DOCSIS 4.0, and future services without significant CPE cost increases is an attractive concept. We look forward to learning more about Puma 9 and evaluating its potential within our network."
Puma 9 is currently available to broadband operators and OEM partners developing next-generation DOCSIS gateways and eMTA solutions. Additional product and partner announcements are expected throughout 2026.
